input.question: Does putting two engines on the same aircraft give it double the thrust?
input.ground_truth: Yes, thrust will double so long as the engines are far enough apart to avoid interacting with each other. Acceleration, top speed and other proformance indicators will not double and may even decreace due to the added weight and drag of a second engine however.

Question: Does putting two engines on the same aircraft give it double the thrust?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a toy car, and you put two batteries in it instead of one. The car might go faster because it has more power, right? It’s kind of like that with airplanes and engines.

If you put two engines on an airplane instead of one, the airplane can get more “push” to move forward. This “push” is called thrust. But just having two engines doesn’t always mean the airplane will go exactly twice as fast or have exactly double the push. Sometimes the airplane is designed so that two engines work together better, and sometimes it’s a little more complicated. But usually, yes, two engines can give the airplane more power to go faster or carry more stuff!
